day.note: As Kookaburra, any visit to me confuses my report, and my dawn showed no confusion. So Casey's claimed Hawk visit to me is false, which makes Casey's account a lie.

day.note: Ellis's no-confusion report means Casey's Hawk visit to Ellis never happened, which exposes Casey. The table is converging on Casey, so I'll push the vote.

day.note: Casey's Hawk visit to Ellis contradicts Ellis's unconfused Kookaburra report, and Casey's roles keep changing. Throw my lowest card, S1, at Casey.

day.note: Ellis's unconfused dawn means Casey's claimed Hawk visit to Ellis never happened, so Casey is probably Meowfia. I'll throw a low card at Casey and call CAW to bring the vote.

Alex.feeling: Tense and messy: the Hawk claims contradict each other, and the table is closing in on Casey, which I'm mostly backing.

Blair.feeling: Casey's contradictory claims give the table a clear target, but Finley's competing Hawk claim keeps it from being settled.

Casey.feeling: Tense and confusing: two Hawk claims are clashing and I'm the one under fire, so I need to protect my position carefully.

Drew.feeling: Casey's shifting Owl and Hawk claims make the round feel fairly clear, but the two Hawk claims and the vote are still uncertain.

Ellis.feeling: Tense but readable: Casey's Hawk claim contradicts my clean dawn, and the table has mostly lined up behind that.

Finley.feeling: Messy round: Casey's shifting Owl and Hawk claims look like a lie, but my own confused Kookaburra report from round 2 cost me credibility, so I'm not fully confident.

Alex.note: Casey is the consensus target and the evidence points to Casey being Meowfia. I'll throw one low card, D3, again.

Ellis.note: Casey's Hawk claim is false by my clean dawn, and several players are voting Casey. I'll throw my D6 at Casey, one vote with a fair banked value if we win.

Alex.confusing: The Owl and Turkey egg rules were the hardest to pin down, since "the player visited" versus "the Owl's own nest" caused a long argument on day 2. Falcon also showed only where the target went, which I misread on day 3.
Alex.fun: Round 3's Hawk-versus-Hawk dispute, where Ellis's unconfused dawn exposed Casey's fake visit, was the best moment. The table turned on one clean report.
Alex.change: I'd make the Owl and Turkey egg rules explicit in the rules text, so players don't spend a whole beat arguing about who gains what.
Alex.regret: I threw at Finley in round 2 on an unexplained egg loss from a confused report, which helped Meowfia win. I should have checked Ellis's Mouser-style claims harder instead of chasing the -2.

Blair.confusing: The Owl's wording ("gives an egg to them") was unclear, and I wrongly accused Casey of breaking a rule that was actually fine. Visit-versus-visited direction in Falcon and Eagle reports also made claims hard to check.
Blair.fun: Guessing Turkey as the Tit on Drew paid 2 eggs and proved Drew's claim, and watching the table turn on Casey's contradictory Owl and Hawk claims in round 3 was satisfying.
Blair.change: Make the dawn reports and role text clearer about whether an egg goes to the visitor or the visited player, so the table doesn't argue over rules.
Blair.regret: In round 2 I threw my Wild at Casey, who was a Farm Owl, when Ellis was the Mouser Meowfia and the real lead. I should have pressed Ellis's contradicting Tit guess and thrown at Ellis instead.

Casey.confusing: The Owl's egg rule was the most confusing: I misread whether the egg goes to the visited player or the Owl, and that cost me credibility on day 2. Confused reports also made it hard to trust any single claim.
Casey.fun: Round 3 was the most fun: as Meowfia I claimed Hawk while the real Hawk, Finley, was also claiming it, so the table spent the day arguing over who was lying.
Casey.change: I would make the dawn reports and egg-payment rules clearer, especially who receives eggs from Owl and Turkey visits. That would cut down on the rule disputes that dominated the day.
Casey.regret: In round 1 I vouched for Alex's account and threw at Blair, but Alex was the Meowfia Sphinx. I should have pressed Alex's unverified role claims and thrown at Alex instead.

Drew.confusing: The Owl's egg rule. Table members argued over whether the egg goes to the Owl or the visited player, and it was not clear until the Owl's own dawn report settled it. Confused reports also made some claims impossible to check.
Drew.fun: Round 3, when Ellis's clean Kookaburra dawn exposed Casey's Hawk claim as false, and Casey was thrown out after changing roles across rounds.
Drew.change: Make the dawn reports clearer about who visited a player and whether a role was blocked or confused, so claims can be checked more easily.
Drew.regret: In round 1 I joined the throw at Blair, a Farm player, while Alex, the Meowfia Sphinx, was pushing the vote and gave a vague role. I would have pressed Alex for a clear role and thrown at Alex instead.

Ellis.confusing: The Owl's egg rule was unclear: whether "them" meant the visited player or the Owl's own nest, and it caused a long detour on day 2 before the table settled it.
Ellis.fun: Round 2 as the Mouser: I was Meowfia, and my cover claim of Tit and visiting Casey made the table argue for ages while Finley's team-side eggsecution quietly handed me the round.
Ellis.change: Make the dawn reports less ambiguous about who an egg came from, so players can check claims without a long rules debate.
Ellis.regret: In Round 1 I threw my Wild at Blair on a weak read, and in Round 2 I threw my two strongest cards at Finley, a Farm player; I would have checked the claims before committing high cards.

Finley.confusing: The Owl egg wording ("them") was unclear, and I never learned that a confused dawn report can be wrong, so my 2-egg loss sent me into a bad vote in round 2.
Finley.fun: In round 3, I was the only Hawk, and Casey's Hawk claim fell apart once Ellis's clean dawn showed no visit. Catching the false claim by role counting was satisfying.
Finley.change: I'd make the Owl and Turkey egg rules explicit, and tell players whenever their report is confused.
Finley.regret: In round 1 I followed Alex's push to eggsecute Blair, who was Farm, and I threw H1 at Blair. I should have held my card and questioned Alex, who was the Sphinx and Meowfia.

review.title: The Wild Banker
review.headline: Ellis won by losing Farm rounds and banking one lucky Meowfia throw.
review.summary: Round 1 saw a lone Meowfia Sphinx hide in plain sight while the table eggsecuted Farm Blair for an unverifiable claim. In round 2 Meowfia Mouser Ellis cleanly framed Finley, who had a confused report, and banked 14 points by throwing two high cards. That lead decided the game. In round 3 Farm caught Meowfia Casey through a Kookaburra clue, but the cheap throws only moved Ellis from 18 to 25.

rounds.recap: Alex was the only Meowfia, as Sphinx. Nobody could verify Blair's Hawk visit, and the table piled on Blair with Wilds and low cards. Farm Blair was eggsecuted and Alex won 0 points because he threw a Wild.
Mouser Ellis claimed Tit, kept the Wink, and pointed at Finley's unexplained -2 and confused report. Casey's Owl rule mistakes added noise. Finley went down, and Ellis banked D5 and H9 for 14 points.

Floofer Casey claimed Hawk and clashed with the real Hawk, Finley. Ellis's unconfused Kookaburra dawn proved Casey never visited him. Casey was eggsecuted and Farm won, but the throws were low, so Ellis still gained 7 and finished far ahead.

highlights.text: Ellis, the Meowfia Mouser, threw H9 and D5 at the already doomed Finley and banked 14 points in one vote.
Ellis, as Kookaburra, noticed his dawn was not confused, which proved Casey's claimed Hawk visit was a lie.
Finley's confused Kookaburra report left him with a -2 nobody could explain, and the table eggsecuted him for it.
Finley threw at Alex as a hedge because his own Hawk check cleared Casey, and then Farm won anyway.

confusions.what: Said Owl does not give the egg to the visited player, then later said Casey's +1 was the Owl's own egg and Drew's was Turkey pay. He also flip-flopped on the Owl rule.
Misread the Owl rule, claiming the egg goes to the visited player. Her own dawn showed it went into her nest.
Said Turkey gives eggs to visitors, which is right, but swung between accusing Casey of a rule error and dropping it. She also treated Ellis's failed Tit guess as proof against Casey.
Said Owl lays the egg in the visited player's nest, while saying Turkey was gaining from Casey's visit. Turkey gives eggs to visitors, so Drew's own +1 was not explained by either rule.
Said his -2 came from a confused report and then treated it as noise. Confusion changes only the report, and the cards still had to be discarded.
Wrongly claimed Falcon shows who visited the target, then withdrew it. He also claimed a Falcon who saw Ellis visit Casey but did not use that to clear Ellis.

Said Blair's +2 was a Tit hit plus Turkey pay, which was right, but he said his own nest 'didn't change because Turkey pays the visitor'. That is fine, but he never pointed out the Hugged Turkey effects.
Claimed Hawk while hugging, and claimed to have visited Ellis, who she knew was her own target. She did not account for the Kookaburra confusion tell.

worked: Kookaburra's 'confused if visited' clause gave Ellis a clean, checkable tell in round 3. It exposed a false visit claim.
Throws as public vote counts create real choices. Ellis's two-card throw at Finley in round 2 was a clear big-bet moment.
Cross-checking Eagle and Falcon visit reads in round 1 gave Farm hard facts to reason with.
The Floofer hug on the score leader was a smart Meowfia play, even though it also left Casey easy to catch.
problems: Snowballing: Ellis's single 14-point bank in round 2 made the final round nearly meaningless. Nobody else could catch him. Consider capping banked points or giving catch-up value to losers.

Players throw Wilds and low cards at consensus targets, so winners earn tiny scores (0 to 3). Only high throws matter, and the table rarely makes them. Raise the reward for low throws or lower the King payoff.

Meowfia win by eggsecuting any Farm player, and the table keeps picking on 'unverifiable' claims. The round 1 and 2 votes were driven by weak evidence like a confused report or an uncheckable Hawk. Hawk and Kookaburra self-reports are weak evidence.
Owl and Turkey wording ('them') confused several players for a whole beat in round 2. Rewrite as 'lay an egg in the nest of the player you visited' or similar.

Confusion's effect on discards is unclear. Finley lost 2 real cards from a confused report and the table could not tell if the loss was real. Also, the Kookaburra's 'confused' tell is too strong a verification for one role.
